# UniFlow — full product facts

UniFlow is a shared workspace for team conversations and follow-through. It keeps channels, reviewed decisions, ideas, tasks, goals and leads in one environment, so the next step stays connected to the discussion behind it.

Positioning: Work with the context behind the task.
Descriptor: AI Communication & Collaboration
Stage: Available for guided evaluation

## Mandatory availability statement
Available for guided evaluation. Some AI and advanced workspace screens use sample behaviour; external AI providers need configuration. A demo is not proof of production readiness.

## Who it is for
- Business owners running several projects
- Project leads handling handovers
- Growing teams whose ideas get lost in chat

## How it works (four stages)
1. Discuss — Keep project messages in channels.
2. Review — Accept or reject proposed decisions and ideas.
3. Assign — Give a task an owner, status and priority.
4. Revisit — Return to stored context when the question comes back.

## What makes it different
- Conversation → reviewed record → task continuity in one environment
- Explicit accept or reject review — proposals are never committed automatically
- Shared provenance: records keep their relationships to the conversation behind them

## Architecture
Layers: People and roles → Channels and work records → Review and task services → Stored events and relationships.
Boundary: Optional external AI providers are configured and policy-gated; device push delivery remains unfinished.

## Capability status (from the repository review)
- Registration and session lifecycle [Implemented]: Sign-up and sign-in sessions
- Organisation and member administration [Partial]: Workspace members and roles
- Project workspace [Implemented]: Projects as the frame for work
- Channels and memberships [Implemented]: Channels for a project or shared topic
- Messages and threaded context [Implemented]: Stored message history and threaded replies
- Presence and live events [Implemented]: Live collaboration events and presence
- Meeting lifecycle [Partial]: Meeting records and lifecycle actions; live video or audio not verified
- Conversation wrapping and extraction [Partial]: Can propose decisions and ideas; the default uses a sample AI provider
- Review decisions [Implemented]: Accept or reject proposed decisions
- Idea capture and task promotion [Implemented]: Keep ideas; promote useful ones into tasks
- Task lifecycle [Implemented]: Task owner, status and priority
- Goals, objectives and milestones [Implemented]: Goal hierarchy and milestone progress
- Lead pipeline [Implemented]: Record leads and change their stage
- Knowledge graph [Backend only]: Relationships are stored; the visual graph uses hand-authored sample nodes
- Semantic retrieval and ask [Partial]: Search and ask need evaluation with configured providers
- Model routing and privacy policy [Implemented]: Provider routing and privacy rules for optional external AI
- Default model provider [Sample behaviour]: The demo AI is a deterministic sample provider
- In-app inbox [Implemented]: In-app notification inbox
- Device push [Not ready]: Push to phones is not ready
- Cockpit and event metrics [Implemented]: A cockpit view of event metrics
- Transactional outbox [Implemented]: Reliable internal event delivery (technical)
- Brainstorm, debate and simulator [Concept screen]: Concept screens
- Agent, prompt and automation administration [Concept screen]: Concept screens
- Mobile client and web mobile showcase [Partial]: Mobile direction, partial
- Revenue concept screen [Sample data]: No forecast or sales improvement promised

Status meanings: "Implemented" means the path exists in the reviewed product; it is not a claim of production scale.

## Evidence
A local 12-stage core-loop exercise covered the areas below. It used deterministic sample AI. It validates a local path — not real-model quality, production scale, customer results or independent certification.
Areas covered: Messages, Extraction-shaped output, Persisted insights, Relationships, Retrieval, Notifications, Cockpit results.

## Pricing
No public price. A written scope and price is provided on request before any purchase decision.

## Claims UniFlow does not make
- A fully autonomous company operating system
- Replacing every tool your team uses
- Production-proven AI accuracy
- Live push notifications to phones
- A verified live knowledge-map dashboard
- Customer counts, testimonials, logos, certifications, uptime, response times, prices or launch dates

## Frequently asked questions
Q: Is this another team chat app?
A: Team chat is one part of it. The product also holds reviewed decisions, ideas, tasks, goals and leads. Its main value is keeping discussion and follow-through close together.

Q: Can we replace every tool with UniFlow?
A: That has not been established. Start with one workflow and check the features, integrations and access controls your team needs.

Q: Can we use it for meetings?
A: Meeting records and lifecycle actions exist. Live meeting media has not been verified.

Q: Will reminders arrive on our phones?
A: The in-app notification inbox is implemented. External device push delivery is not ready in the reviewed source.

Q: Does AI automatically make decisions for us?
A: No. Proposed insights need review. The default evaluation uses sample AI output; a real provider must be configured and checked separately.

Q: Can we use our own AI provider?
A: Provider routing and privacy rules exist. Availability and quality depend on configuration and separate validation.

Q: Is the knowledge graph live?
A: The backend stores relationships. The current visual graph screen uses hand-authored sample nodes and should be shown as a concept preview.

Q: What should we test first?
A: Use a single project: create a channel, discuss a topic, review a decision and create a task. Check that the team can find the context again.

Q: Is there a public price?
A: No public price is listed. Ask for a written scope and price for your requirements before making a purchase decision.

Q: Is UniFlow ready for production use?
A: UniFlow is available for guided evaluation. Some AI and advanced workspace screens use sample behaviour; external AI providers need configuration. A demo is not proof of production readiness.

Q: What should we bring to a walkthrough?
A: One anonymised example of the work, the people who handle it and the result you need. Avoid passwords, account keys, private customer records or employee details.
